newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries off lows at midday, moving with dlr.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries off lows at midday, moving with dlr.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices were off session lows at midday, but still posted losses as the market fluctuated in line with dollar movements, participants said.

"It's the dollar," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and money market economist at Dean Witter Reynolds. "With nothing else going on, the market has moved pretty much in lockstep fashion with the dollar."
At midday, the 30-year Treasury bond was down 10/32 to 99-16/32, yielding 6.66 percent. Two-year notes were down 2/32 to 100 even, yielding 5.87 percent.

Besides the dollar, the market's two main considerations on Monday were Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress, scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday, Feb. 26-27, and the Treasury's two note auctions, set for Tuesday and Wednesday.
The Treasury will sell $17.5 billion in two-year notes on Tuesday and $12.5 billion in five-year notes on Wednesday.
Sluder said the two-year notes should not pose a big problem for the market because the auction takes place a day before the Greenspan testimony, subjecting positions to less "headline risk."
